Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>

    Release build: let a self-hosted Mac take the Mac jobs
    
    GitHub's macos-15 runners cancelled the 2.0.1 release's Mac app builds
    three times in a row, each with "The job was not acquired by Runner of
    type hosted even after multiple attempts". Kenneth chose to build them on
    his own Mac: "Use my Mac".
    
    - The repository variable JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER, when set, sends the Mac
      app builds and the universal-app job to a runner labelled
      [self-hosted, <its value>]. Unset, everything runs on macos-15 as
      before. inputs.os stays macos-15, so the deps cache keeps its key.
    - The step that deletes every other Xcode_*.app and the simulator caches
      with sudo now runs only on GitHub's machines (RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT).
    - The signing step makes a temporary keychain the user's default and the
      only one in their search list. It now saves both first, and a step that
      runs even after a failure puts them back and deletes the temporary
      keychain.
    
    Checked with actionlint, and the save-and-restore parsing dry-run on a
    Mac: it reads back the login keychain as the default and both keychains
    in the list.

# build host. Normalize once here, before anything links against the dep:
    # give the dylib an @rpath id and teach the interpreter to find it relative
    # to itself. Consumers then just need an rpath entry (src/CMakeLists.txt).
    # install_name_tool invalidates code signatures, so re-sign ad-hoc; CI
    # re-signs the whole bundle with the real identity later.
    # ld collapses '//' in -install_name (but not in -rpath) strings, while
    # ${DESTDIR} ends with a slash -- collapse slashes so -change matches the
    # recorded install name.
    string(REGEX REPLACE "/+" "/" _python_prefix "${DESTDIR}/libpython")
    set(_python_dylib "${_python_prefix}/lib/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib")
    set(_python_bin "${_python_prefix}/bin/python${_python_version_short}")
    set(_install_cmd make install
        COMMAND install_name_tool -id "@rpath/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib" "${_python_dylib}"
        COMMAND install_name_tool -change "${_python_dylib}" "@rpath/libpython${_python_version_short}.dylib" "${_python_bin}"
        COMMAND install_name_tool -add_rpath "@loader_path/../lib" "${_python_bin}"
        COMMAND codesign --force --sign - "${_python_dylib}"
        COMMAND codesign --force --sign - "${_python_bin}"
    )
else()
    # Linux/Unix
    # Kept verbatim, no slash normalization (unlike the macOS branch's
    # collapsed copy): the LDFLAGS rpath below is recorded byte-for-byte in
    # the ELF, and the OLD_RPATH handed to relocate_linux.cmake must match it
    # exactly -- both derive from this one variable to make that structural.
    set(_python_prefix "${DESTDIR}/libpython")
    # The rpath points at libpython's real install dir, so the interpreter runs
    # in-tree pre-relocation -- and, critically, it reserves enough RUNPATH
    # bytes for the in-place $ORIGIN rewrite at install time (Flatpak's
    # DESTDIR is the short /app) -- see relocate_linux.cmake.

name: JusPrin build all

# Every platform of JusPrin from one commit, for jusprin_release.yml (a draft
# release) and jusprin_nightly.yml (the nightly-builds pre-release).
#
# Each platform is built by jusprin_release_build.yml; the macos job joins the
# two macOS architectures into the universal app and its disk image. The
# files are left as this run's artifacts named jusprin-*, for the caller to
# collect: the Windows x64 installer and portable zip, the macOS universal
# disk image, the Linux x64 AppImage, and the per-architecture Mac bundles,
# which only feed the universal app.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string
      # Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets JusPrin 1.x
      # used. Windows builds are unsigned.
      sign_macos:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-15
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-15
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: build
    # A self-hosted Mac when JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER is set, as in jusprin_release_build.yml.
    runs-on: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER && fromJSON(format('["self-hosted","{0}"]', vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER)) || 'macos-15' }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -j 1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          # What the steps below replace, for the last step to put back: on a
          # self-hosted Mac these are its owner's own keychain settings.
          security default-keychain -d user | xargs > "$RUNNER_TEMP/default-keychain"
          security list-keychains -d user | xargs > "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      # Puts back the user's default keychain and keychain list, and deletes
      # the signing keychain, even when an earlier step failed.
      - name: Restore the keychains
        if: always() && env.SIGN == '1'
        run: |
          [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list" ] || exit 0
          read -r -a keychains < "$RUNNER_TEMP/keychain-list"
          security list-keychains -d user -s "${keychains[@]}"
          security default-keychain -d user -s "$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/default-keychain")"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          [ ! -e "$keychain" ] || security delete-keychain "$keychain"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

input.command: cat .github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml

result.output:
name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    # GitHub often has no hosted macOS runner free, and cancels a job that gets
    # none within 15 minutes, so the macOS lookup runs on Linux, as in
    # OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml.
    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && 'ubuntu-24.04' || inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
          cache_os: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
          dep_folder: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
        run: |
          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The workspace of a hosted macOS job, where build_deps.yml saved the tree.
          if [[ "$OS" == macos-* ]]; then
            echo "macos_workspace=/Users/runner/work/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      # actions/cache matches the path too, so a Linux lookup for macOS names the
      # macOS workspace.
      - name: Look the cache up
        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.macos_workspace || github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
      compiler: msvc
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    # The repository variable JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER, when set, sends the Mac
    # builds to a self-hosted runner with that label instead of GitHub's
    # macos-15, whose queue can cancel a job that waits too long for a
    # machine. inputs.os stays macos-15, so the deps cache keeps its key.
    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER && fromJSON(format('["self-hosted","{0}"]', vars.JUSPRIN_MAC_RUNNER)) || inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      # The Sentry project the app's error reports go to, read by
      # JusPrin/sources.cmake; kept out of the public repository.
      JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN }}
      # The pages' build, which their error reports carry and their source
      # maps are filed under in Sentry (WebShared/errorReports.ts).
      JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD: ${{ github.sha }}
    steps:
      # A build without it sends no error report or crash, which nobody would
      # notice until reports were needed.
      - name: Require the Sentry key
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -z "$JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN" ]; then
            echo "::error::The secret JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN is missing, so this build would send no error report or crash."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
        run: |
          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
          # selected Xcode. Only on GitHub's machines: a self-hosted Mac is
          # someone's own computer.
          if [ "$RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT" = github-hosted ]; then
            xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
            sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
            sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*
          fi

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        # Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let Sentry give the file and line
        # of each frame; they go into the dSYM below, not into the app.
        run: >-
          ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15 --
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only

      # The line tables stay in the build's object files; dsymutil gathers
      # them into a dSYM for Sentry, and strip -S then drops the executable's
      # pointers to those files. The executable keeps its function names.
      - name: Split the debug information
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          bin="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"
          dsymutil "$bin" -o "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM"
          strip -S "$bin"

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i). Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let
          # Sentry give the file and line of each frame; they are split off
          # below, not shipped.
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      # Sentry files a debug file by the executable's GNU build id, which the
      # split file keeps; without one the two would not match.
      - name: Split the debug information
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          bin=build/package/bin/orca-slicer
          readelf -n "$bin" | grep -q 'Build ID' || {
            echo "::error::$bin has no GNU build id, so Sentry could not match its debug file to it."
            exit 1
          }
          objcopy --only-keep-debug "$bin" build/orca-slicer.debug
          objcopy --strip-debug --add-gnu-debuglink=build/orca-slicer.debug "$bin"

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      # OrcaSlicer.pdb is over 2 GiB, and JusPrin's Sentry (self-hosted 23.1.1)
      # stores no file larger than that: its file table keeps offsets in a
      # 32-bit integer. Mozilla's dump_syms turns the PDB into a Breakpad
      # symbol file, about a quarter of its size, with the same build id and
      # each function's file and line; Sentry shows no inlined frames from it.
      - name: Convert the app's PDB to Breakpad for Sentry
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $zip = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms.zip"
          Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -OutFile $zip `
            https://github.com/mozilla/dump_syms/releases/download/v2.3.9/dump_syms-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip
          if ((Get-FileHash $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'BDF48486220708808A3E00AEC78856EE1CCE096189D47A1E2CB1C635F93BACC7') {
            throw "dump_syms-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip does not have the checksum of dump_syms 2.3.9."
          }
          Expand-Archive $zip "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force build\sentry-breakpad | Out-Null
          & "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\dump_syms\dump_syms.exe" build\src\Release\OrcaSlicer.pdb -o build\sentry-breakpad\OrcaSlicer.sym
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }

      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each
      # executable and library the app ships, filed by its build id, and the
      # debug information split off above (on Windows, the Breakpad file made
      # from OrcaSlicer.pdb and the launcher's own small PDB). The build fails
      # unless Sentry then holds the app's own code's debug information, with
      # file and line (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh). Sentry's address and
      # the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets.
      - name: Upload debug files to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Windows) main=build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll; paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release/orca-slicer.pdb build/sentry-breakpad) ;;
            macOS)
              app="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app"
              main="$app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"; paths=("$app/Contents" "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM") ;;
            *) main=build/package/bin/orca-slicer; paths=(build/package/bin build/package/lib build/orca-slicer.debug) ;;
          esac
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh upload "$main" "${paths[@]}"

      # What lets Sentry name the Agent and Home pages' code in a page error's
      # stack: each page and its source map, filed under this commit. Every
      # platform builds the same pages; the step fails if one differs.
      - name: Upload page source maps to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh upload

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
          retention-days: 7

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide check and
the Sentry secrets, and fails a platform whose debug files or page source
maps did not reach Sentry (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.

- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.

ASSISTANT : Yes, it can be done on GitHub's Macs. I haven't tried it yet; here is what the code shows.

**Why the build picks up Homebrew's library.** Python's build script looks for optional libraries on the machine it runs on. GitHub's Mac images come with Homebrew and its `xz` package already installed. So the build finds Homebrew's `liblzma` and links the `_lzma` module (Python's compression module) against `/opt/homebrew/...`. A Mac without Homebrew has nothing at that path.

The recipe, `deps/python3/python3.cmake`, already handles the same kind of problem for one module. Around line 291 it switches off `_tkinter` with `py_cv_module__tkinter=n/a`, because Homebrew's Tcl/Tk breaks it. The recipe appears to come from upstream OrcaSlicer: its commits carry OrcaSlicer pull-request numbers, but I haven't checked them with `git blame`.

**Two ways to fix it on GitHub's Macs:**

1. **Leave the module out.** Add `py_cv_module__lzma=n/a` next to the tkinter line. That's one line, and `_lzma` is then never built, so nothing links to Homebrew. The cost: `import lzma` fails on every Mac, including Macs where it works today. I haven't checked whether anything in JusPrin or its plug-ins uses `lzma`. My guess is nothing does, but I'd search before choosing this.
2. **Build `xz` ourselves.** Add `xz` as a dependency and point Python at our copy, the way it already gets our OpenSSL. `lzma` then works everywhere, but this is a bigger change to a file owned by upstream OrcaSlicer, and every future upstream merge has to carry it.

**Either way, the first build is slow.** Changing the dependency recipe changes the cache key, so the next GitHub build rebuilds all dependencies for both chips. That takes about an hour more, once.

Two more things:
- The outside-library check (`mac_outside_links.sh`) is so far only on my unlanded branch for your Mac. Landing it in the GitHub build would fail any future build that links Homebrew again, instead of us finding out after a release.
- The check found only `_lzma` in 2.0.1, so this one line or one dependency should be the whole fix.

If you want it, I'd do the first way after a search shows nothing uses `lzma`, and land it with the check, as a fix for the next release. I don't think it needs to hold up 2.0.1, because 2.0.0 shipped with the same link.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Usage: mac_outside_links.sh <folder> [<allowed folder>...]
+#
+# Lists every program and library under <folder> that loads a library from
+# outside macOS (/usr/lib, /System), outside itself (@rpath, @loader_path,
+# @executable_path) and outside the allowed folders, and exits 1 if there is
+# one. A Mac that builds JusPrin can have Homebrew or XQuartz installed, and a
+# build that links their libraries runs there but fails on a Mac without them.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+dir=$1
+shift
+allowed=("$@")
+
+found=0
+while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+  # Only the load commands: a library's own install name is not a load.
+  while IFS= read -r lib; do
+    case "$lib" in
+      /usr/lib/* | /System/* | @rpath/* | @loader_path/* | @executable_path/*) continue ;;
+    esac
+    ok=0
+    for prefix in "${allowed[@]+"${allowed[@]}"}"; do
+      case "$lib" in "$prefix"/*) ok=1 ;; esac
+    done
+    if [ "$ok" = 0 ]; then
+      echo "$file loads $lib"
+      found=1
+    fi
+  done < <(otool -l "$file" 2>/dev/null |
+    awk '/cmd LC_(LOAD|LOAD_WEAK|REEXPORT|LAZY_LOAD|LOAD_UPWARD)_DYLIB$/ { load = 1; next }
+         load && $1 == "name" { print $2; load = 0 }' | sort -u)
+done < <(find "$dir" -type f \( -name '*.dylib' -o -name '*.so' -o -perm -u+x \) -print0)
+
+# A static library loads nothing itself, but its CMake, pkg-config, libtool
+# or wx-config files hand the libraries it needs to whatever links it: a
+# library file's absolute path, or a folder after -L. Those must not be in
+# Homebrew, MacPorts or XQuartz. (A folder a Find module merely searches is
+# neither.)
+outside='(-L|^|[[:space:]"'"'"';=(])(/opt/homebrew|/usr/local|/opt/local|/opt/X11|/usr/X11R6|/usr/X11)/[^[:space:]"'"'"';)]*'
+while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+  links=$(grep -E -o "$outside" "$file" |
+    sed -E 's/^[[:space:]"'"'"';=(]//' |
+    grep -E '^-L|\.(dylib|tbd|so|a|la)$|\.framework' | sort -u || true)
+  if [ -n "$links" ]; then
+    echo "$links" | sed "s|^|$file links |"
+    found=1
+  fi
+done < <(find "$dir" -type f \( -name '*.cmake' -o -name '*.pc' -o -name '*.la' -o -path '*/wx/config/*' \) -print0)

# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.

# Running it again skips what is already done.

# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the seven

#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.

label=jusprin-release-mac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Turns OrcaSlicer's universal app into JusPrin.app and puts it in a disk image.
#
#   macos_package.sh <OrcaSlicer.app> <version> <output dir>
#
# OrcaSlicer's build names the bundle OrcaSlicer.app with OrcaSlicer's bundle
# identifier, icon and a "JusPrin <build id>" version string. This copies it to
# JusPrin.app and sets JusPrin's identity before anything is signed, because
# editing Info.plist afterwards would break the signature.
#
# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed with the
# Developer ID certificate in MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID (already in the keychain)
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. Otherwise the app
# gets an ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only.
set -euo pipefail

source_app="$1"
version="$2"
out_dir="$3"

script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd -- "${script_dir}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
entitlements="${repo_root}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${repo_root}/scripts/retry.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
stage="${work}/dmg"
app="${stage}/JusPrin.app"
dmg="${out_dir}/JusPrin_Mac_universal_V${version}.dmg"
mkdir -p "${stage}" "${out_dir}"
cp -R "${source_app}" "${app}"

plist="${app}/Contents/Info.plist"
buddy=/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy
set_key() {
    "${buddy}" -c "Set :$1 $2" "${plist}" 2>/dev/null || "${buddy}" -c "Add :$1 string $2" "${plist}"
}
set_key CFBundleIdentifier io.obico.jusprin
set_key CFBundleName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleDisplayName JusPrin
set_key CFBundleShortVersionString "${version}"
set_key CFBundleVersion "${version}"
set_key CFBundleGetInfoString "JusPrin ${version}"
cp "${repo_root}/resources/jusprin/images/JusPrin.icns" "${app}/Contents/Resources/images/JusPrin.icns"
set_key CFBundleIconFile images/JusPrin.icns
plutil -lint "${plist}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml signs: --deep misses the bundled Python
    # runtime, and notarisation rejects any Mach-O file without the hardened
    # runtime signature, so each one is signed, then the bundle last.
    # The main executable is left to the bundle's signature: signed on its
    # own, codesign checks the jusprin-mcp beside it, which the universal
    # join left unsigned, and fails with "code object is not signed at all".
    sign() {
        codesign --force --options runtime --timestamp --entitlements "${entitlements}" \
            --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "$@"
    }
    main_executable="${app}/Contents/MacOS/$("${buddy}" -c "Print :CFBundleExecutable" "${plist}")"
    machos=()
    while IFS= read -r f; do machos+=("$f"); done < <(
        find "${app}" -type f -print0 |
            xargs -0 file --no-pad --mime-type -- |
            grep -v ' (for architecture ' |
            grep ': application/x-mach-binary$' |
            sed 's|: application/x-mach-binary$||' |
            grep -vxF "${main_executable}"
    )
    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    sign "${machos[@]}"
    sign --verbose "${app}"
else
    codesign --deep --force --sign - "${app}"
fi
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "${app}"

ln -sfn /Applications "${stage}/Applications"
retry hdiutil create -volname "JusPrin" -srcfolder "${stage}" -ov -format UDZO "${dmg}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    codesign --force --verbose --timestamp --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${dmg}"
    notary=(--apple-id "${APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT}" --team-id "${TEAM_ID}" --password "${APP_PWD}")
    # notarytool exits 0 when Apple rejects the image, so read the status and
    # print Apple's report, which names each file it rejected.
    result="$(xcrun notarytool submit "${dmg}" "${notary[@]}" --wait --output-format json)"
    echo "${result}"
    if [ "$(plutil -extract status raw - <<<"${result}")" != "Accepted" ]; then
        xcrun notarytool log "$(plutil -extract id raw - <<<"${result}")" "${notary[@]}"
        exit 1
    fi
    retry xcrun stapler staple "${dmg}"
fi

rm -rf "${work}"
echo "${dmg}"
